memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When Joshua had grown old, the Lord said to him, "You are now very old, and there are still very large areas of land to be taken over." - Josh 13:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joshua is an old man now. The great battles are behind him, the major kings defeated, and he might reasonably expect to hear, "Well done, your work is complete." Instead God says something surprising: there is still very much land to be taken over. Even at the end of a long and faithful life, the task was not fully finished.

This is a gentle and honest word for all of us. On this side of heaven, the work is never entirely done. There is always more ground to claim, more of God's promises to enter into, more growth still ahead. That truth could feel discouraging — but it need not. It simply means God is not finished with us, whatever our age or stage.

Notice too that God does not scold Joshua for what remains undone. He states it plainly and then, as we will see, moves forward with the next step: dividing the land. God works with us where we are. Age and weariness do not disqualify us from usefulness; God had more for Joshua to do even in his final chapter. And the One who begins a good work in us is faithful to carry it on to completion — a completion that rests on Christ, not on our running out of strength (Phil 1:6).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you ever feel your best days of usefulness are behind you?
- What "land" might God still be calling you to enter, whatever your age?
- How does it comfort you that God, not your strength, completes the work?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, whatever my age or weariness, thank You that You are not finished with me. Give me courage to keep entering the good things You still have for me. Amen.
